sources.title: Gemma 3 model card
sources.evidence: Describes open pretrained and instruction-tuned Gemma 3 variants, text/image inputs, text output, multilingual support and 128K context for 27B; identifies IT as instruction tuning. Reopened October 27, 2026: no separate numerical active-count convention is supplied for the 27B IT model.

sources.title: Introducing Gemma 3: The Developer Guide
sources.evidence: Dated March 12, 2025. Launches 1B, 4B, 12B and 27B in both pretrained and instruction-tuned versions and reports function calling, structured output and vision-language input.

sources.title: Gemma 3 Technical Report
sources.evidence: Specifies decoder-only Transformer, GQA and 5:1 local/global attention. Table 1 labels the 27B model with rounded 417M vision, 1,416M embedding and 25,600M nonembedding counts. The shared vision encoder is a SigLIP Vision Transformer; raw and quantized releases are distinct. Reopened October 27, 2026. Table 5 gives the exact IT model a single nominal 27B entry under a combined params/activated heading, rather than separate total and active rows. Section 3 identifies instruction tuning of the pretrained model; this does not justify copying the precise full checkpoint total into active parameters.

sources.title: Official Gemma 3 27B IT model repository
sources.evidence: Exact google/gemma-3-27b-it instruction-tuned model, distributed under Gemma terms. The public model card is readable; raw configuration and index requests require acceptance of the repository gate. Reopened October 27, 2026 to confirm the exact original IT variant; later QAT and specialized fine-tunes are distinct.

sources.title: Pinned official Gemma 3 27B IT repository metadata
sources.evidence: For the pinned official revision, safetensors metadata reports 27,432,406,640 BF16 elements and the same total, with no other tensor dtypes. Lists Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration, gemma3 architecture and google/gemma-3-27b-pt base model. Fresh October 27, 2026 metadata retrieval reconfirms the same revision, BF16 total and named PT base without downloading weights or repeating the tensor census.

sources.title: Pinned official Gemma 3 27B IT file metadata
sources.evidence: Lists 12 original safetensors shards, the index and a 972-byte config. Official config blob identity matches the accessible Second State config copy; model and config file commits are dated March 12, 2025. File metadata was inspected, not whole weight shards.

sources.title: Public copy of original Gemma 3 27B IT configuration
sources.evidence: Third-party config copy, independently matched byte-for-byte by Git blob identity to the pinned official repository tree. Specifies BF16, 62 text layers, width 5376, MLP 21504, 32 query/16 KV heads of dimension 128, and a 27-layer SigLIP tower of width 1152 with MLP 4304 and no pooling head. It is configuration evidence, not evidence from quantized weights.

sources.title: Transformers v4.50.0 Gemma 3 implementation
sources.evidence: Defines all language and multimodal projector parameters, including four RMSNorm vectors and two head-dimension Q/K norms per decoder layer. Declares tied output embeddings; RoPE frequency buffers are nonpersistent. Projector has a 1152 by 5376 matrix plus a 1152-element normalization vector.

sources.title: Transformers v4.50.0 Gemma 3 configuration defaults
sources.evidence: Supplies omitted official-config defaults: vocabulary 262208, tied word embeddings, bias-free text projections, and maximum positions 131072.

sources.title: Transformers v4.50.0 SigLIP implementation
sources.evidence: Defines learned patch and position embeddings, attention/MLP weights and biases, layer norms and final vision norm. The position-ID buffer is nonpersistent, and vision_use_head=false excludes the pooling head.

sources.title: Official Google Gemma PyTorch model configurations
sources.evidence: The get_config_for_27b_v3 function independently confirms 62 layers, width 5376, head/MLP dimensions and 131072 maximum positions for Gemma 3 27B. Its unpadded tokenizer vocabulary differs from the Hugging Face conversion default; the checkpoint count here follows the latter.

sources.title: Gemma Terms of Use
sources.evidence: The custom terms govern use, modification and distribution of Gemma models, including associated model parameters.

sources.title: Google Gemma models for ADK agents
sources.evidence: Explicitly names gemma-3-27b-it and says Gemma 3 lacks native function calling; dedicated ADK classes implement workarounds. This qualifies the launch claim of function-calling capability rather than proving an inability to produce calls from instructions.

sources.title: Official configuration download (access limited)
sources.evidence: Official raw/blob/resolve config and index downloads returned HTTP 401; individual tensor headers were not independently read. Exact count is instead reconstructed from matched config and implementation and reconciled with official metadata.

sources.title: Pinned Gemma 3 checkpoint conversion implementation
sources.evidence: The exact 27B configuration specifies width 5376, 62 layers, 32 query/16 KV heads, and the no-pooling SigLIP tower. Vision-enabled conversion appends 64 sampled embedding rows, increasing vocabulary to 262208 and adding 344064 checkpoint parameters. These are conversion-created entries, not original trained embeddings.

sources.title: Gemma release chronology
sources.evidence: The current chronology lists March 10, 2025 for Gemma 3, conflicting with the contemporaneous March 12 developer announcement. The explicit dated launch is retained.

sources.title: Qwen3 Technical Report — Table 16
sources.evidence: Independently reopened October 27, 2026. Table 16 explicitly assigns the exact Gemma-3-27B-IT column 27B Activated Params and 27B Total Params in a text-benchmark comparison. This establishes Qwen’s nominal benchmark convention, not a Google specification or precise count of participating tensors.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 for retrospective parameter disclosures. Table 4 lists Gemma 3 27B with nominal 27B in a combined parameter column; benchmark tables compare its text and vision results without a separate active-count row. The explicit active-count discussion concerns Gemma 4’s MoE model, not this Gemma 3 checkpoint.

sources.title: Gemma 4 model card — Gemma 3 comparisons
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact Gemma 3 27B comparison column gives benchmark results, without a total or active parameter row. The card’s 3.8B active figure belongs only to Gemma 4 26B A4B and is not transferred.

name.note: Exact official 27B instruction-tuned variant; distinct from PT and later QAT variants.

developer.note: Developed by Google DeepMind; Google is the catalog developer name.

family.note: Gemma 3 belongs to the Gemma family.

release_date.note: Dated primary launch explicitly includes the 27B instruction-tuned model. Repository creation on March 1 is not public release evidence. The later release chronology says March 10; retained March 12 from the contemporaneous launch and recorded the conflict.

open_weights.note: Official weights are distributed under the custom Gemma terms, with a license-acceptance gate.

license.note: Custom Gemma Terms of Use; not an Apache or unrestricted open-source license.

parameters_b.note: Complete unique parameter count reconstructed as 27,009,346,304 language + 416,866,032 vision + 6,194,304 projector/norm = 27,432,406,640, exactly matching pinned official BF16 metadata. Tied 262208 x 5376 embeddings counted once; nonpersistent RoPE/position-ID buffers excluded. BF16 weights are not packed quantization. Nominal 27B is not the full multimodal total. Config is a third-party copy matched to official file identity; raw tensor headers remain gated. The pinned converter independently confirms these dimensions and adds 344064 embedding entries during conversion; the pre-conversion implementation total is 27432062576. Fresh October 27 pinned BF16 metadata reconfirms the retained total; the nominal benchmark size does not replace this complete checkpoint count.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 27B active parameters under Qwen’s published Table 16 text-benchmark convention for the exact IT model. This is not an exact per-token census or a separate Google disclosure. It does not assert every vision/projector parameter participates in each generated token; no component scope is inferred from the rounded table value.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only language Transformer with GQA and interleaved local/global attention, plus a SigLIP vision Transformer and multimodal projector.

context_window.note: 128K tokens; explicit numeric maximum-position setting is 131072.

modalities.note: Model-card native modalities. Video examples operate through sequences of images and do not establish a separate native video encoder.

reasoning.note: Sources report general reasoning performance, but do not explicitly establish or exclude a dedicated reasoning/thinking capability for this exact checkpoint. Clear the unsupported false flag.

tool_call.note: Google explicitly advertises function calling. ADK clarifies that Gemma 3 lacks native function-call support and uses prompting/parsing workarounds; true here records the documented model capability, not a native Gemini API protocol or executed tools.

description.value: Instruction-tuned Gemma 3 model for multilingual text generation and image understanding.
description.note: Plain factual description of the exact variant; removes the unnecessary largest-model comparison.

patch.description: Instruction-tuned Gemma 3 model for multilingual text generation and image understanding.
patch.notes: Total includes 27,009,346,304 language, 416,866,032 vision and 6,194,304 projector parameters, with tied embeddings counted once. The language count includes 344,064 entries added during Hugging Face conversion. Pinned metadata and implementation agree; raw tensor headers were inaccessible. Active 27B follows Qwen’s nominal text-benchmark convention, not an exact per-token count or a separate Google disclosure; vision participation varies with input. Google supports function calling through prompting and output parsing. The March 12 launch announcement conflicts with a later release log saying March 10.
